stages.name: Boom
stages.title: Boom
stages.sub: The student can identify the five characteristics of a boom phase of the trade cycle.

steps.q: The economy is at the very top of the trade cycle, above its normal trend. Compared with a normal year, is real GDP growing quickly or slowly?
steps.right: Very quickly, faster than the trend
steps.hint: Think about where this sits on the cycle: the peak, not the recession.

steps.q: Firms are producing and selling as fast as they can to meet demand. Do they need to hire more workers or lay them off?
steps.hint: If firms are struggling to keep up with orders, what do they do about staff?
steps.pre: So firms hire more, and unemployment is

steps.q: Shops are full of customers all wanting to buy, but shelves are struggling to be restocked in time. What tends to happen to prices?
steps.hint: When demand keeps outrunning supply, what happens to the price shops can charge?

steps.q: Sales are strong, workers feel secure in their jobs, and firms are planning to expand. How do households and businesses feel about spending and investing?
steps.wrong: Nervous and wanting to cut back
steps.hint: Would people who feel secure in their jobs cut back on spending, or keep spending?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: With firms straining to produce more than they normally could and factories running flat out, is actual output above or below what the economy can sustainably produce?
steps.right: Above what it can sustainably produce
steps.wrong: Below what it can sustainably produce
steps.hint: You already know what it's called when actual output exceeds potential output.
